description: Generate a routed, laid-out network diagram from topology text (Graphviz DOT, Mermaid, CSV, CDP/LLDP neighbour output from most switch vendors, a FortiLink topology dump, Containerlab, Meraki or UniFi JSON, or an Ansible inventory — every format is listed in the drawbridge://guide resource) and export it. Drawbridge decides where the lines go; you decide what connects to what. HOW TO GET A PRECISE RESULT: device output the user pasted IS the source — pass it unchanged, never rewritten as DOT. When you write DOT yourself: set `kind=` on EVERY device so it draws as the real thing rather than a neutral box (firewall, waf, ips, vpn-gateway, proxy, nac, router, switch, l3-switch, load-balancer, wifi-ap, wlc, … — full list in the drawbridge://guide resource). Put `speed=` on every cable ("10G", "1G"), and `link=` where the cable MEANS something (ipsec, trunk, lag, wan, mgmt, wireless, conduit, fieldbus, ha). Never set `pos=`, `width=` or `height=`: Drawbridge lays out and routes — placing devices yourself is what makes a diagram look generated. READ THE `notes` IN THE RESULT AND FIX YOUR SOURCE: they name each line that was skipped or adjusted, and an unrecognised kind silently becomes a plain box otherwise. Iterate until the notes are empty. CHOOSING `kind`: `drawio` when the user will open or edit the drawing (this is usually what they want, and it is the only one they can change); `svg` to embed in a document or a page; `png` to show inline in a chat; `drawio.svg` / `drawio.png` for ONE file that is both: a picture a wiki, a README or Obsidian shows, with the whole drawing inside it, which Drawbridge and draw.io open for editing; `describe.json` to READ a drawing back and reason about it; `csv` / `netbox.csv` for a cable schedule and `netbox-devices.csv` for the hardware; `dot` to hand the topology on; `clab.yml` to turn the design into a Containerlab topology you can deploy; `html` for one self-contained page that opens offline in any browser — every page, zoom, search and the cable schedule — to hand a drawing to someone without Drawbridge (save it as a file; it is too large to show in a chat). Results carry `name`: a suggested basename for this diagram. Write every file for one diagram into its own directory named after it — <name>/<name>.drawio, <name>/<name>.svg, <name>/<name>.cables.csv — so two diagrams never share a directory.

name.description: Basename to use for this diagram instead of the one derived from its content. Slugified; wins over the document’s own name.
